subject: music-therapy
intro: Music therapy leads into allied health roles where structured activity is the treatment — recreational and occupational therapy and rehabilitation counseling — alongside board-certified music therapy practice itself.

roles.title: Recreational Therapists
roles.what: Plan, direct and coordinate medically-approved recreation programs in hospitals and nursing homes — activities such as music, arts, sports and social events — assessing each patient's condition and recommending the right activity as therapy.
roles.where: The course's assessment-then-treatment arc matches the role: referral and assessment methods, selecting interventions by goal, and adaptation of activities for neurologic rehab, dementia care and developmental populations.

roles.title: Occupational Therapists
roles.what: Assess, plan and organise rehabilitative programs that build or restore daily living skills and independence for people with disabilities or developmental delays, adapting environments and modifying the tasks that block them.
roles.where: The clinical populations unit — neurologic rehabilitation, autism and developmental disabilities, mental health — is OT's caseload, and the treatment-planning unit's goal setting and method adaptation is OT's core craft.

roles.title: Rehabilitation Counselors
roles.what: Counsel people to maximise independence and employability while coping with personal, social and vocational difficulties from illness, injury, aging or disability, assessing needs and designing rehabilitation programs.
roles.where: Foundations' research base on how music affects brain and body, the client-strengths focus in assessment, and the documentation, ethics and interprofessional-practice unit map directly onto counselling's assessment and care coordination.
